subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call follow-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Carter <jon.carter@finops.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call follow-ups

Thanks for the call earlier — good discussion. Recap and next steps below so we have a single place to track requirements for the Dedicated capacity perf validation.

Summary of FinOps Analytics requirements:
- Latency SLOs:
  - Short responses (<= 64 tokens): p95 <= 120 ms
  - Long streaming responses (average output ~2k tokens): p95 <= 800 ms end-to-end (streaming chunks should start within 150–200 ms)
- Throughput / concurrency:
  - Baseline sustained throughput target: 400 requests/min (roughly ~7 rps) for average mix, but burst to 800 requests/min (13+ rps) during spike windows
  - Expected concurrency (simultaneous open sessions): 60 concurrent streams; peak concurrency 120
- Model & payload characteristics:
  - Average prompt length: ~120 tokens
  - Average completion length: 200–2k tokens (50% of calls are streaming long outputs)
- Requirements:
  - Dedicated reserved throughput (SLA-backed) — customer needs predictable p95 behavior, not just best-effort
  - GPU comparison: they asked for guidance on A100 vs H100 sizing and cost tradeoffs for our quantized/pipeline runtime
  - Security/compliance: SOC2 controls and data residency in US (we covered this on the call)

Requested deliverables from Redwood:
1) SE perf validation report comparing A100 vs H100 for their workload (int8/float16 where applicable), including token/sec, per-node concurrency, and p95 latency estimates.
2) Suggested Dedicated configuration: reserved capacity (node counts), autoscale/burst policy config, and expected monthly cost delta.
3) A 1-hour validation run using a sample of their prompts (they'll share a sanitized dataset) — target dates below.

I cc'd Aditya to own the detailed perf numbers and run the benchmark run with the FinOps sample. Aditya — can you confirm the load profile you need from Jon / Priya (QPS, exact concurrency distribution, and sample dataset format) and whether the benchmarking PDF I attached covers the initial comparison matrix?

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_benchmarks_Q2_2027.pdf (summary), mutual_action_plan_FIN-2345.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0139

Thanks Marissa — that recap is super helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side to make sure the validation maps to our production profile: 

- Prompt / completion distribution: ~60% of calls are short (<= 64 tokens) for UI helpers and search, ~40% are long (>= 800 tokens) for report generation. Of the long calls, roughly 75% are streaming.
- Peak: our absolute peak is closer to 20 rps sustained for 90s blocks during batch runs; normal peak windows are more like 10–12 rps.
- Concurrency: the 60 concurrent streams figure is accurate for our steady state; 120 is a hard cap for peak events.
- Dataset: Priya will share a sanitized set of 500 representative prompts and a few larger report-generation prompts by EOD Monday.

If you can show a recommended config that meets the streaming p95 target while maintaining those peaks (including a brief cost delta), we can move to an internal approval fast-track. Also confirm whether the streaming API supports chunked SSE with latency under 200ms (we need to show our UX team).

Jon
Jon Carter | Head of Platform, FinOps Analytics
jon.carter@finops.io | +1 650-555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Carter <jon.carter@finops.io>, Priya Rao <priya@finopsanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call follow-ups

Hi Jon / Priya — thanks, received. Quick technical answers and a summary of the benchmarking evidence (see attached PDF for full numbers):

1) Streaming latency behavior: our streaming API supports chunked SSE and server-side flushing. In our tests, initial token flush latency (time-to-first-chunk) is typically:
   - H100 (int8/optimized kernel): 60–120 ms for short prompts, 120–180 ms for larger contexts when KV cache warms.
   - A100 (fp16/optimized): 90–180 ms for similar workloads.
So H100 gives lower TTF (time-to-first-chunk) in our quantized paths. End-to-end p95 for long streaming responses is dominated by per-token generation speed, which we captured in the attached PDF.

2) Throughput / sizing guidance (summary recommendation that maps to your SLOs):
   - Option A (performance / lower latency): 4 x H100 nodes reserved.
     - Expected behavior: meets short-response p95 <= 120 ms and long-streaming p95 <= 700–800 ms at 60 concurrent streams with bursts to 120 using our autoscale/burst config.
     - Throughput: ~2.1x token/sec vs a single A100 node for quantized int8 models (benchmark depends on model size and quant profile).
   - Option B (cost-conscious): 8 x A100 nodes reserved (fp16 path).
     - Expected behavior: meets short-response p95 ~120–200 ms and long-streaming p95 ~800–1100 ms at 60 concurrent streams; higher node count compensates for lower per-node throughput.
   - Notes on cost: H100 hardware (~+30–45% per-GPU cost) but fewer nodes required; A100 requires more nodes and higher overall management overhead. We'll include estimated monthly cost deltas in the MAP spreadsheet.

3) Reserved throughput & autoscale parameters (suggested starting config):
   - reserved_qps: 8 rps (per-customer route) x cluster sizing to reach baseline throughput; for your stated baseline we recommend reserving capacity to support 400 req/min sustained.
   - burst_policy: allow burst to 2x reserved for 60s windows (burst to handle 800 req/min spikes).
   - per-node concurrency: configure per-node max concurrency 12–16 streams (dependent on model size) to avoid head-of-line blocking.
   - KV/prefix caching: enable automatic prefix cache for common prompts (we can preload top 50 templates you share).

4) Benchmark artifacts: attached redwood_dedicated_benchmarks_Q2_2027.pdf includes:
   - test harness: tokenized sample workload, end-to-end p95 measurements, token/sec comparisons across H100/A100 with int8/fp16 profiles, and cost-per-million-token estimates.
   - quick take: H100 int8 showed ~2.1x token/sec vs A100 fp16 on our 7B–13B family test models; for 70B+ models differences narrow and memory/partitioning become dominant.

Next steps I need from your team to scope the run:
- Final sanitized prompt set (Priya) — prefer JSONL with prompt_id and expected max output length.
- Target model family (we ran these on the 13B family; let me know if you want 70B or custom)
- Target date/time for a 1-hour validation run (proposal below)

Proposed validation windows:
- Tue 2027-04-26 10:00–11:00 PT (preferred)
- Wed 2027-04-27 14:00–15:00 PT

I'll coordinate with infra to spin up a temporary cluster with both H100 and A100 nodes so we can run back-to-back comparisons using your sanitized sample.

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_benchmarks_Q2_2027.pdf

Cheers,
Aditya Rao | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
